title: Yellow-clad solidarity attendance at Lideta court and reported supporter detentions
location: Federal High Court, Lideta Division, Addis Ababa
organizer: Supporters and family members of Jawar Mohammed, Bekele Gerba and co-defendants; formal organizer unknown
participants_original: Wardheer/Addis Standard body reports at least/about 80 supporters detained; caption says up to 80. Physically abusive police treatment also affected unrelated yellow-clad pedestrians.
threshold_50_evidence: Reported 80 court supporters may represent one physical gathering, but lower-bound crowd size of people making a public own-state demand is unresolved; do not equate detainees and passing pedestrians with qualifying demonstrators.

start_date.summary: Jan 28 article says supporters were detained at yesterday’s hearing; Feb 17 body explicitly names Jan 27. Search-only later account has conflicting relative-date wording.

location.summary: Lideta federal court premises and excluded courtroom entry.

organizer.summary: Supporters/family attendance in solidarity; no named coordinating organization.

demands.summary: Solidarity with accused established; crowd’s own public demands not stated explicitly. Prisoners’ demands are a separate action.

participants.summary: About/at least 80 supporters reportedly detained, caption up to 80; no safe qualifying-crowd lower bound.

state_response.summary: Supporters reportedly detained and taken to Balcha police station; bodily abuse wording is nonspecific, all other seven-response categories remain unknown.

end_date.summary: No explicit physical closure established; later hearing/strike dates are not this assembly’s end.

protester_violence.summary: No explicit state-directed physical violence assessment.

notes: Clothing and attendance show solidarity, but the read sources do not explicitly describe this crowd voicing a state-policy demand. Defendants’ later prison-strike demands cannot be automatically assigned to attendees. Jan 28 contemporaneous report describes yesterday, and Feb 17 account identifies Jan 27 hearing; unread Feb 2/3 syndication snippet says previous day relative to Jan 27 strike, requiring date-conflict check. Arrests are attributed to the reported solidarity attendance, not to prior 2020 detentions; generic physical abuse does not establish beatings or shootings. February court attendance and street protests do not establish continuous occupation.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people participate in a public state-directed protest, rather than only attending court or passing nearby?
Recover original Addis Standard body when ordinarily accessible and resolve Jan 26/27 date wording.
What was the physical end of the court solidarity action?
Which police methods affected actual participants, separately from pedestrians?

title: Planned Jan 31 Balderas demonstration prohibited before verified execution
location: Addis Ababa; precise planned assembly site not verified
scope: planned domestic demonstration; foreign-city plans kept separate
threshold_50_evidence: Not established for a qualifying physical public gathering.

start_date.summary: Planned Sunday Jan 31; no actual executed onset verified, hence null.

demands.summary: Future agenda presses own federal authorities on detainees, protection and land policy, with separate Sudan-border issue.

participants.summary: No actual attendance; property and affected-population counts excluded.

state_response.summary: Pre-gathering prohibition documented separately; seven assembly-response fields unknown.

end_date.summary: No executed physical assembly or closure established.

notes: Intended date Jan 31, 2021 is a planned date, not actual onset. Police Jan 29 prohibition and organizer newspaper do not establish that a crowd assembled. Domestic demands concern political detention, protection and land policy; Sudan-border agenda alone would not establish home-grown targeting. Condominium numbers and newspaper electoral alliance discussion are not attendance. No police dispersal code from preemptive prohibition without physical assembly.
open_questions: Did any domestic public gathering actually occur despite the ban?
Recover contemporaneous after-Jan31 reporting, fluent Amharic review and actual turnout if execution occurred.

title: January West Wellegga anti-OLF demonstration reports awaiting original episode evidence
location: West Wellegga, Oromia; exact town or assembly unverified
scope: retrospective group of reports; episode number unresolved
organizer: Residents described in government-associated media; organizer unverified
threshold_50_evidence: Not established for a qualifying physical public gathering.

start_date.summary: January retrospective reference lacks episode-level onset; cited Jan 15 is publication, so null actual start.

demands.summary: Denunciation of OLF/Shane attributed, own-state protection demand unverified.

participants.summary: No contemporaneous size or lower bound; period incident totals do not count people.

notes: ACLED report explicitly mentions January anti-OLF demonstrations and cites EBC Jan 15; this establishes a positive discovery lead, not a codable single assembly. The EBC publication date cannot become an event start. Target could be insurgent group only or a state protection demand; neither inferred. No arbitrary per-city/day splitting. Insecurity Insight’s broader January–March reference may overlap but does not identify the same action.
open_questions: Recover EBC Jan 15 original and any other contemporaneous regional reporting.
Separate actual own-state demands from pro-government/anti-insurgent mobilization.
Verify actual crowd size, date, locality, organization, response and episode boundaries.
